newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat prices slip after weekend rain.
newsitem.headline: French wheat prices slip after weekend rain.

text.p: French wheat prices eased on Monday on improved prospects for the 1997 harvest after the weekend's rain and forecasts for more rain and cooler temperatures in the next few days, dealers said.
Trade was very thin ahead of what should be another slow week due to a public holiday on Thursday, they said.

Wheat for May delivery into Rouen was bid at 880 francs per tonne and offered at 890 francs per tonne, excluding carry, down 10 francs on Friday. New-crop wheat into Rouen was offered at 910 francs for August delivery and at 905 francs on August-December delivery but there were no buyers.
On Matif milling wheat futures the September 97 expiry was bid at 903 francs per tonne and offered at 910 francs per tonne but there was no trade.
Meteo France said Sunday's and Monday's rain would bring 10-20 millimetres across the country and that wet weather would last until at least Thursday.
The prediction was likely to please farmers, whose crops have suffered from a three-month dry spell.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
